questions: Did s-bend line_loss_events fall below 0.95, and did s-bend progress rise above 0.858 with more than 13 of 20 finishes?
Did steering_oscillation stay under about 0.35 on the oval, s-bend and slalom with body_length 0.10? If it rose, did the shorter body or the lower yaw inertia cause it?
Did the slalom finish any trials, or did its progress rise above 0.23 with line_loss_events below 1.0?
Does the oval still finish 20 of 20 with max_error near 0.018?
If the slalom still leaves the line at max_error 0.06, is the limit now controller gain, so the next step should be a controller change rather than geometry?

intent: Continue the lower-yaw-inertia step that iteration 5 validated. Shorten body_length from 0.12 to 0.10 m with mass held at 0.6 kg, keeping the sensor layout, 12 mm footprint, wheel_track 0.09 and wheel_radius 0.03 unchanged, so the only geometric change is body length. This should give faster heading response on the s-bend and slalom and push s-bend line losses further below 1.0. If oscillation rises above about 0.35 on any track, the next step is to restore body_length to 0.12.
learning: Iteration 5 showed that reducing yaw inertia was the first geometry lever to break the s-bend limit (2 to 13 finishes, losses 1.0 to 0.95). The slalom did not respond, which suggests a separate limit on alternating bends. Next, check whether the further inertia cut gives more s-bend gain, and whether the slalom's max_error stays at the floor. If it does, geometry has done most of what it can for the development tracks, and the remaining gains should come from the controller.
rationale: Iteration 5 (score 580, the best so far) cut yaw inertia by shortening the body from 0.16 to 0.12 m and reducing mass from 0.8 to 0.6 kg. The s-bend improved sharply: 13 of 20 finishes (up from 2), progress 0.858 (from 0.68), line losses 0.95 (below the 1.0 threshold) and steering oscillation 0.298 (under 0.35). The oval stayed at 20 of 20 with max_error 0.018 and oscillation 0.217. The slalom remains the weak track: 0 of 20 finishes, progress 0.23, and 1.0 line losses per run. Its max_error is 0.063, at the off-track floor, so it still loses the line at the edge of the band. Iteration 3 showed that narrowing wheel_track to 0.09 with the 12 mm footprint and y 0.07 holds the oval well, so the sensor layout is kept. The Integrator's rule for this step is met: s-bend losses are below 1.0 and s-bend oscillation is under 0.35, so the next step is a lower-inertia move. I set body_length to 0.10 m, the lower end of the allowed range, with mass held at 0.6 kg. Yaw inertia falls from about 0.00146 to about 0.00121 kg·m². Sensor positions, the 12 mm footprint, wheel_track 0.09, wheel_radius 0.03 and body_width 0.12 are unchanged, so the only change is body_length. Expected result: s-bend progress and finishes improve further (line losses at or below 0.95, progress above 0.86), and the oval keeps 20 of 20 finishes. Slalom progress may rise modestly, but it is likely still limited by turn authority and the controller. Risk: a shorter body may increase jitter. If steering_oscillation rises above about 0.35 on any track, I will restore body_length to 0.12, which keeps the mass benefit.
